svg.title: Separate Cancellation Causes and Recover Failed Payments
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-retention-and-payment-recovery-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Separate Cancellation Causes and Recover Failed Payments; subtitle: Diagnose churn, validate first value, configure payment recovery, and inspect cohort economics.; caption: RonBuilds, Hormozi on Business Beast Mode, Freemius, Dodo Payments, Recurly, Gravy, and Ask a VC supply the operating checks.; assumptions note: Week headings are planning slots, not a shared implementation schedule reported by these practitioners. Recurly's recovery windows and Gravy's 30-day claim remain separate observations, not weekly performance promises.; note: Recurly reports median recovery of 47% for 1–7-day windows and 57.7% for 15–21-day windows. Gravy reports average recovery of 51% within 30 days. Neither establishes a universal recovery target or a like-for-like vendor comparison.; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Separate voluntary and involuntary churn; deliverable: A cohort breakdown separating deliberate cancellations from failed-payment losses, following RonBuilds.; gate: Keep gross losses visible even when expansion improves net churn, as Ask a VC recommends.; week: Week 2; title: Validate the first-value event; deliverable: An activation check and hands-on onboarding approach grounded in RonBuilds and Hormozi on Business Beast Mode.; gate: Confirm that the proposed activation event distinguishes retained users from departing users; RonBuilds warns that a universally completed event is not enough.; week: Week 3; title: Configure retries and payment updates; deliverable: Retries, reminders, and an easy card-update path as Freemius describes, with Dodo Payments distinguishing fixable failures from stolen-card failures.; gate: Inspect payment-status conditions and unsuccessful branches as Ecom Mastery recommends. Recurly advises experimenting with recovery windows for the business.; week: Week 4; title: Evaluate recovered value and follow-up cost; deliverable: A recovery assessment that considers Gravy's dedicated human follow-up approach alongside automated recovery.; gate: Check cohort value before personalized price offers and keep retargeting cost below customer value, following RonBuilds.
